newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MALONE LOVES MOTORCYCLE'S ROAR, HATES FIREWORKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MALONE LOVES MOTORCYCLE'S ROAR, HATES FIREWORKS.

text.p: The Utah Jazz's Game 3 hero Karl Malone loves the roar of his motorcycle but hates the fireworks his team set off before hosting their first NBA Finals game.
At practice Saturday for the next day's Game 4, Malone, who lived up to his Mailman nickname by delivering a victory, expanded on the relaxation he gets riding any one of his three motorcycles.
"Sometimes when things are a little bit tough, I do that. I get the bike and ride for about 30 minutes," he said.
In fact, he arrived at Friday's game on his motorcycle.

"I wanted to own one for 20 years and no one ever would let me get one. My mom wouldn't, my college coach wouldn't, when I first got here... until I got to be the Mailman Larry never would let me," he said, referring to Jazz owner Larry Miller.
"It's just a release as far as I'm concerned."

Riding the motorcycle gives him the same kind of escape as his hunting and fishing trips. "It's just gettting away. I've got four or five guys I ride with and we can ride a couple of hours without even talking to each other, riding together."
He treasures his solitude. "It's just being out, outdoors, being away from everybody," said Malone.
Even though you never can really get away from people while riding, he said, "You can always brush them off like you don't hear them because the pipes are too loud."
Would he again let his son choose which bike he would take to the game Sunday? "It worked last time, I'll let him pick it again. I know which one he'll pick, too."
Would he shine it up for the occasion? "Yeah -- well, somebody will," he said, laughing.
He may be a country boy at heart, but he is rich and no fool. "It's like mowing lawns. If you don't have to do it, you won't."
Asked about the deafening indoor fireworks display the Jazz put on before Game 3, Malone joined the Chicago Bulls in opposition.
"I don't really like it, only thing it did was make my kids cry. My kids are not big on fireworks."
He added: "The 10, 15, 20 thousand dollars they spent they could do some other things. That's their way of getting us going, I guess."
